title: Pad Thai
subtitle: Thai stir-fried rice noodles with egg, beansprouts, and peanuts
excerpt: Rice noodles stir-fried in a sweet and sour tamarind sauce with eggs, beansprouts, and spring onions, served with a scattering of crushed peanuts and a wedge of lime.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad Thai is Thailand's national noodle dish, created in the 1930s and 1940s as part of a government campaign to promote rice noodles and Thai nationalism. The dish was designed to be cooked and sold from street carts and uses a simple, balanced sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar that is characteristic of Thai cooking. Authentic pad thai is cooked in a very hot wok, one portion at a time; the noodles are stir-fried with egg, protein (tofu, shrimp, chicken, or a combination), and beansprouts, then finished with peanuts, spring onions, and lime at the table. The tamarind paste provides the essential sour note: rice wine vinegar can substitute but the flavour is different.

recipeTools.notes: A large wok or the widest frying pan you have.

content.text: Soak the rice noodles in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking: this softens them without making them sticky. They will finish cooking in the wok. Do not over-soak or they will become mushy. Mix the sauce ingredients together before you start: once the wok is hot, everything happens quickly and there is no time to measure. Cook in two batches if making more than two portions; a crowded wok steams rather than fries.

content.text: Mix the tamarind paste, fish sauce, caster sugar, and soy sauce together in a small bowl. Heat a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the oil.
Fry the garlic for 20 seconds. Add the prawns and cook for 1 minute. Push to one side. Crack in the eggs and scramble loosely, then fold through the prawns.

Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and just tender. Add the beansprouts and half the spring onions and toss for 30 seconds. Divide between plates. Scatter with peanuts, remaining spring onions, chilli, and coriander. Serve with lime wedges.
